newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine leader pledges peaceful power transfer.
newsitem.headline: Philippine leader pledges peaceful power transfer.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Sunday pledged a peaceful transfer of power to his successor after presidential elections in May next year.
The ex-army general repeated his vow to step down at the end of his six-year term in June 1998 after opposition accusations that he planned to seek a second term.

Ramos made the pledge shortly before the Supreme Court is to hand down its verdict on a bid by a citizens' group to be allowed to initiate a referendum to amend the constitution and lift the limits on terms of incumbent officials.
The present constitution limits the president to one term.
The court in March rejected moves to amend the constitution but the group has appealed for a reconsideration. Judiciary sources said the court could decide on the appeal when it meets on Tuesday.

"When we hold national and local elections next year...the world will witness the orderly transfer of power from this administration to a new one," Ramos said in a speech to government and business leaders.
Ramos, who has nourished the country's economic rebirth with his liberalisation policies, presented to the meeting "a wish-list of what we want the Philippines to be."

The list, he said, called for making the Philippines "a food basket of Asia, a maritime and shipping power, a commercial hub, an energy exporter, a regional financial centre (and) a southeast Asian shopper's super-market."
